summary.text: A 72-year-old woman was admitted with gradual onset of nonspecific visual changes. General physical examination was unremarkable and fundoscopic examination did not yield much. Conventional angiography revealed two aneurysms at the ophthalmic segment of the left internal carotid artery.

Both aneurysms were treated with a pipeline embolization device without coils under general anesthesia. The device did not open well at the anterior curve of the siphon because the parent artery was tortuous, so a balloon was used to straighten it and implantation across both necks was achieved. Aspirin and clopidogrel were given after the procedure, and she was discharged on postoperative day 5 after repeated angiography detected no complications, with the aneurysm totally occluded before discharge.

Two months after the operation she was rushed to the emergency room with bilateral conjunctival congestion, and CT showed intracranial hemorrhage at the left temporal lobe. DSA established a left direct carotid cavernous fistula with multiple draining veins, and the rupture point was proximal to the pipeline device rather than the aneurysmal wall or sac.

The fistula was occluded with stent-assisted coils. Post-procedure DSA showed all draining veins eliminated except the inferior petrosal sinus, and she was discharged 2 weeks after the procedure with the hemorrhage absorbed. Two years of follow-up showed the patient well, with no neurological deficits and no recurrence of the fistula.

ambiguities.text: The abstract dates the emergency return as two months after discharge, whereas the case body dates it two months after the operation. Discharge was on postoperative day 5, so the anchors differ by about five days; the case-body wording is used and no single date is inferred.

ambiguities.text: The authors call the rupture a delayed spontaneous event rather than iatrogenic, but also state they cannot rule out that technical manipulation of the tortuous parent artery caused a focal traumatic weakness and a delayed tear, propose PLED radial force and flow dynamics as a mechanism, and the abstract lessons state outright that manipulation resulted in the weakness and delayed tear. These attributions are mutually inconsistent; no cause is asserted here.

evidence.quote: This mean that the rupture of the cavernous segment of the ICA in our case was a delayed spontaneous event instead of an iatrogenic event.
Manipulation of the tortuous parent artery resulted in a focal traumatic weakness in the artery and subsequently a delay tear.

we cannot rule out the fact the dual nature OSA coupled with a tortuous parent artery led to several technical manipulation which could have resulted in a focal traumatic weakness in artery resulting in a delay tear
We are also of the view that, radial force exerted by the PLED coupled the flow dynamics in vessel led to rupture of the vessel in our case.

ambiguities.text: The source describes the cavernous ICA rupture and the direct carotid cavernous fistula separately; the authors refer to "the rupture point or the fistula" without stating whether they are one lesion, so they are kept as separate facts and not merged.
